transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-18
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Evan Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Jared Collins (CTO, Atlas Health), Priya Rao (Platform Eng), Alex Martinez (ML Eng), Sana Li (PM)
Link to artifacts: runbook draft (placeholder) https://redwood.app/runbooks/atlas-poc, benchmarks sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/atlas-poc-benchmarks

[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Jared: Jared here.
[00:07] Priya: Priya on the line.
[00:09] Alex: Alex here.
[00:11] Sana: Sana.
[00:13] Maya: Maya from Redwood.
[00:15] Evan: Cool. Agenda today: finalize canary strategy, confirm monitoring and rollback criteria, and assign runbook owners.

[02:10] Maya: Quick recap of last week — we ran the shadow traffic for the chat flow at 10% and saw p95 around 280 ms for the small model variant, p99 spiked to 620ms during the cold KV-cache misses, so we recommended warming and some prefix caching. There was one transcription hiccup in the logs where model id came through as "redwood-lite" in the sheet, that was manual tagging on our side.

[04:30] Alex: Yeah, the spikes were mostly when we hit unseen prefixes; caching looks like the right call. For rollout I want to clarify — are we doing a canary by route or by percent? Our product team wants to route only billing-check flows first.

[05:10] Evan: Good Q. Two approaches: route-by-route (safer) or percentage-based A/B. For Atlas we suggested route-by-route for the first canary: billing-check and reconcile flows, then widen to search and note-summarization. That reduces blast radius.

[06:20] Jared: Route-by-route makes sense. We need to minimize user impact; billing-check is high-precision. If something degrades, rollback needs to be instant. What's the rollback plan?

[06:40] Maya: Rollback criteria we proposed: sustained increase in error rate >1.5x baseline for 5 minutes, p95 increase >1.5x baseline for 5 minutes, or model hallucination rate on golden prompts exceeding threshold. Rollback action: instant traffic switch to previous stable model or route to hosted fallback. We can automate with policy but initial cutover will be manual with 2-operator approval.

[08:05] Priya: On automation — can we hook that into our PagerDuty? We want automatic alerting to on-call and an automated change that stops canary traffic if thresholds breached.

[08:30] Maya: Yep, Redwood supports webhook alerts to PagerDuty/SNS and can trigger route-policy changes. We recommend manual confirmation for the first two canaries, then enable automated rollbacks after a successful run.

[10:00] Alex: Monitoring — what dashboards will we get? We need p50/p95/p99, tokens-per-request, throughput, error rates, model variant distribution, and KV cache hit-rate. Also retention of logs for compliance — 90 days minimum.

[10:30] Maya: We'll share the dashboard link. Default dashboards include latency percentiles, QPS, model-level token counts, and tail-latency. For KV cache we emit hit/miss per-shard. Audit logs can be shipped to your S3 with encryption; retention configurable.

[12:00] Jared: That brings up security: SSO and KMS. We need SAML SSO for console access, RBAC for role separation, and customer-managed KMS keys for log encryption. SOC2 compliance is also a requirement for procurement.

[12:40] Evan: Understood — Redwood supports SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations. We'll attach SOC2 Type II report and the security whitepaper after this call.

[14:10] Sana: For runbooks, we want a playbook that includes: canary start steps, smoke-checks (golden prompts and service tests), rollback steps, and post-mortem template. Can we get that as editable doc?

[14:40] Maya: Yes, we'll share an editable runbook template. It will include checklist items, smoke test commands, and the exact thresholds for automated actions.

[16:00] Alex: About golden prompts — we have a set of 120 prompts used across flows. We'll catalog and mark which are critical. We'll share those by Friday.

[16:20] Evan: Great. For cutover timing, are you expecting a maintenance window or a live gradual rollout?

[16:40] Jared: Prefer gradual live rollout during low-traffic window. We can plan a 2-hour window where we ramp from 0 to 20% route traffic over 30 minutes, observe for an hour, then 50% then full.

[17:10] Maya: That ramp plan aligns with best practice. We'll propose concrete timestamps and a canary checklist: initial smoke, telemetry baseline compare, 30-minute soak, golden-prompt pass rate check.

[19:00] Priya: On capacity — if we go with dedicated Redwood capacity for predictability, what's the burst model? We need headroom for morning peaks.

[19:30] Evan: Dedicated provides baseline vCPUs/GPUs with a burst pool. Pricing estimate will include baseline throughput and an hourly burst rate. We'll send a cost model showing token/unit economics vs hosted per-token pricing.

[21:00] Alex: Any limits on model variants during canary? We might want to test a quantized variant and a higher-precision variant for fallback.

[21:25] Maya: You can pin model versions per route. We support automatic fallback to a compatible variant if model isn't available. For A/B you can split traffic between two variants and compare metrics. Just watch token cost differences.

[23:00] Evan: Let's nail concrete rollback criteria now so they're in the runbook. Maya, can you read back the thresholds?

[23:10] Maya: Sure. Rollback triggers:
- Error rate >1.5x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes
- p95 latency >1.5x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes
- Golden prompt failure rate >2% in a rolling 10-minute window
Manual override to immediately stop canary traffic.

[25:00] Jared: Fine. For alerts we want severity mapping and escalation 0/15/30 min. Can we map to our PD escalation policy?

[25:20] Maya: Yes, we'll provide a mapping doc and example PD integration.

[27:10] Priya: Observability — we want tracing hooks to correlate user request IDs to generated tokens. Is that possible?

[27:35] Maya: Yes — inject the request ID header and we output trace id in the logs. We also support distributed tracing integrations (Zipkin/Jaeger) via OTLP.

[29:00] Alex: A couple of concerns from infra: where does the KV cache live? If it's shared across tenants or per-tenant? We need to understand data residency for cached prefixes.

[29:30] Maya: For Private/Dedicated you can have tenant-isolated cache. Hosted uses multi-tenant caching but caches are encrypted at rest. If you'd like per-tenant isolation we recommend dedicated pools.

[31:10] Evan: Okay, back to schedule. Proposed plan:
- 2025-03-20: Redwood shares runbook + canary checklist + pricing estimate
- 2025-03-21: Atlas provides golden prompts + shadowing window time
- 2025-03-24: SE runs load tests and shares telemetry
- 2025-03-26: Cutover planning call and pick exact cutover window

[33:00] Sana: What's included in the runbook doc? Will it have sample rollback scripts?

[33:20] Maya: Yes, sample CLI commands to switch route policies, how to flip model pinning, and playbook notes for on-call. We'll include runbook YAML and sample PD runbook entries.

[35:40] Alex: About canaries — do we also want a small A/B test for the higher-quality variant on a subset of internal users for subjective quality testing?

[36:00] Evan: Good idea. We can run an internal-only A/B with 2% of traffic or shadow traffic to internal users; collect quality metrics and human evals.

[37:15] Priya: For compliance retrieval — audit logs, who can access them, and retention needs to be locked. We need them unreadable without KMS access.

[37:35] Maya: We'll enable customer KMS for your logs, and RBAC will limit access to read logs. We can set retention and export policies per your compliance requirements.

[39:10] Jared: Anything else on cost? I want the tradeoffs spelled out: hosted cheaper up-front but more variable; dedicated predictable but capex-like commit.

[39:35] Evan: Exactly. We'll provide a spreadsheet with sample monthly token volumes and cost curves for each option including burst scenarios and cost per successful user action.

[41:00] Sana: Are there any special legal procurement steps for the dedicated offer? We might need a separate SOW.

[41:20] Evan: Yes, Dedicated and Private often use a separate contract/SOW and include SLA terms. Legal will start the draft after the pricing estimate if you choose to proceed.

[43:00] Alex: SE load test detail — what parameters will you run?

[43:20] Maya: We'll run 2k concurrent synthetic users across the billing-check flow, ramp test for 30 minutes, and record p50/p95/p99, error rates, KV miss rates, and token throughput. We'll also run the same with a quantized variant to compare DLQ rates.

[45:05] Priya: For observability, can we get raw request traces for a limited window for debugging?

[45:20] Maya: Yes, we can export a limited retention window of raw traces to your S3 during the canary period. We'll redact PII if needed.

[47:10] Evan: Quick recap and owners — Maya to share runbook and dashboards by 3/20; Evan to send pricing; Alex to share golden prompts; Jared to confirm SSO/KMS contacts. We'll schedule cutover planning on 3/26.

[48:00] Jared: Sounds good. A quick note — we might want to run a dry-run cutover with internal traffic only.

[48:15] Evan: Agreed. We'll include a dry-run checklist.

[49:40] Alex: Minor transcription note — earlier you said "redwood-lite" which matches the model alias, but in our codebase it's called rwd-lite; just make sure mapping is consistent.

[50:00] Maya: Noted, we'll align aliases and confirm mapping in the runbook.

[51:30] Sana: Any blockers right now? From our side it's mainly gathering golden prompts and confirming PD integration.

[51:55] Jared: From infra, we need to confirm KMS policy before the canary. We'll try to get that in the next two days.

[52:30] Evan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the runbook and schedule.

[53:00] Meeting end.
